testName: Class B Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should you turn off your turn signal?
questions.explanation: Keep your turn signal on the whole time you are turning. Turn it off only when the turn is complete.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while going downhill, what is your best option to stop?
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, look for an escape ramp. This is the safest way to stop your vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You get an extra point against your score.
You automatically fail the entire test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire test.
questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and use three points of contact when exiting. On a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly means you automatically fail the basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is being aggressive toward you?
questions.explanation: Do not react to angry gestures from other drivers. Avoid eye contact and do not race them.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: Plan ahead and allow extra time for traffic delays. This reduces frustration that can lead to aggressive driving. Also drive at safe speeds, keep a safe following distance, and avoid making gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs replacing.
Because water collects in the tanks from compressed air.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because water collects in the tanks from compressed air.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and oil that build up in the tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: Why do some air brake systems add alcohol?

options.text: To make the brakes work without squeaking.
To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
To prevent people from breathing the air.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to help stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: What condition should engine belts be in?
questions.explanation: Check engine belts for tightness and excessive wear. The safe amount of give varies by vehicle, so learn what is correct for yours.

questions.question: What is bracing used for in a trailer?
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing stop cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking goes in front, back, and on the sides. Bracing goes from the top of cargo down to the floor and sides.

questions.question: What should you check on power steering hoses?

options.text: Make sure they connect to the battery.

questions.explanation: Inspect power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: If you begin a left turn before reaching the center of an intersection, what may happen?

options.text: You will likely complete the turn safely.
You may hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
Other drivers will move their vehicles to let you turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may hit other vehicles with the left side of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always reach the center of an intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle.

questions.question: During the driving test, if the route does not include a railroad crossing, what may happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything about railroad crossings.
The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Even if the test route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would cross railroad tracks at a pretend location.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The weight the manufacturer states a vehicle can hold when fully loaded.
The maximum weight a vehicle can pull.
The minimum weight a vehicle can haul.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight the manufacturer states a vehicle can hold when fully loaded.
questions.explanation: The Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) is the maximum loaded weight of a single vehicle as stated by the manufacturer.

questions.question: If mirrors are dirty before you start driving, what should you do?

options.text: They will become clean after driving a short distance.

questions.explanation: Before starting a trip, check your mirrors and windshield for dirt. Clean them so you can see clearly while driving.

questions.question: Water collected on a roadway can cause:
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen when water collects on the road surface.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of a vehicle's air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems include an air compressor, storage tanks, gauges, a low air pressure warning device, and spring brakes. An air filter is not part of the air brake system.

questions.question: Which of the following helps prevent hydroplaning on wet roads?

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your tires have good tread depth.
questions.explanation: Good tire tread helps prevent hydroplaning. Worn tires or low tire pressure increase the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads. If you start to hydroplane, release the accelerator and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: Why are roads especially slippery when rain first begins to fall?

options.text: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
The water has not yet washed away the dirt and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water mixes with oil and grease on the road.
questions.explanation: When rain first falls, it mixes with oil and grease on the road surface, creating a slippery film before water washes it away.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.explanation: Check your tires before every drive. Rust around wheel nuts is a sign that they may be loose.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to spot potential vehicle problems?

options.text: Watch the gauges on the dashboard.
Use your senses to notice changes.
Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check critical items only at the start and end of a trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during a trip, not just at the beginning and end. Watch the gauges, check mirrors, inspect tires and lights, and use all your senses to catch problems early.

questions.question: How should you put out an electrical fire?
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: When should you check cargo being transported?

options.text: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, then every three hours or 150 miles. Also check it every time you stop. You are responsible for keeping cargo safe during the entire trip.

questions.question: What should you do when backing with a trailer?

options.text: You should not back up in a straight line.
You should not correct drift until you are far off course.
You should frequently pull forward to reposition the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should frequently pull forward to reposition the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Pull forward to reposition your vehicle whenever needed while backing. Fix any drift right away by turning the steering wheel in the direction of the drift.

questions.question: Which behavior shows you may be an aggressive driver?

options.text: Slow down and maintain a reasonable following distance.
Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, plan for delays, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, and do not make hand gestures that could upset other drivers.

questions.question: What happens to a vehicle's speed when traveling downhill?
questions.explanation: Gravity causes a vehicle to speed up when going downhill.

questions.question: What is important when loading a trailer?

options.text: Place as little weight as possible over the axles.
Place an appropriate amount of weight over the axles.
Not be concerned with how the cargo's weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place an appropriate amount of weight over the axles.
questions.explanation: Each axle needs the right amount of weight—not too little and not too much. Wrong loading affects steering, reduces tire grip, and can damage the axles.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of tire failure?
questions.explanation: Tire failure signs include a loud bang, heavy thumping, or vibration. If steering feels heavy or the rear fishtails, stop and check your tires.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, yawning, rubbing eyes, daydreaming, forgetting what you've driven, missing exits, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, or feeling restless and irritable.

questions.question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact to better communicate with them.
Not move out of their path of travel.

questions.explanation: If confronted by an aggressive driver, get out of their way if possible. Do not make eye contact, as it may provoke them. Do not react to their actions.

questions.question: How do you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn on the engine and apply the trailer hand brake.
Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
Remove wheel chocks and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Your low pressure warning light must work properly. After the system charges, test it by rapidly pressing and releasing the brake pedal. This releases air, and the warning should come on when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: When making tight turns, what should a driver do?

options.text: Open their door to see better.

questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors while driving. Check them especially when changing lanes, turning, merging, or making tight turns.

questions.question: How should you brake if your vehicle's ABS is broken?

options.text: Brake normally. Your brakes will still work.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally. Your brakes will still work.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle still has normal brakes without ABS. Drive and brake as you normally do. Get your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: When starting from a complete stop, a vehicle should:
questions.explanation: Make sure your vehicle does not roll backward when you start moving forward from a stop. This prevents hitting vehicles behind you.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of distraction?
questions.explanation: Driving distractions are physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking with a passenger), or both (like using a handheld phone).

questions.question: How should a truck be parked?

options.text: So it must back up to leave the space.
So it can pull forward to leave the space.

questions.correctAnswerText: So it can pull forward to leave the space.
questions.explanation: You cannot see everything behind you. Backing is dangerous and should be avoided. Park in spaces where you can pull forward when leaving.

questions.question: Where are regrooved tires allowed on a bus?
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires cannot be used on the front of a bus.

questions.question: After changing a tire, what should you do shortly after?

options.text: Stop and check that the lug nuts are tight.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later to check that the lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: How long should it take air pressure to build up in a single air system?
questions.explanation: In a single air system, air pressure should build from about 50 to 90 psi in three minutes.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. Examples include ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning light comes on?

options.text: Keep driving but get the brakes fixed within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop safely right away while you can still control the brakes. Inspect and repair the brakes as soon as possible.

questions.question: People working on a disabled vehicle:

options.text: May focus on repairs and not see traffic nearby.
Do not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May focus on repairs and not see traffic nearby.
questions.explanation: Be careful when driving near people working on a broken-down vehicle. They are focused on the repair and may not notice oncoming traffic.

questions.question: While driving, ____ keeps spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops too low, the spring brakes will activate.

questions.question: A truck tractor built after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: All truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: The Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) does not need to include which of the following?

options.text: Number of meals eaten by the driver

questions.correctAnswerText: Number of meals eaten by the driver
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include trip origin, destination, vehicle identification number, and fuel information. It does not need to include meals the driver ate.

questions.question: While driving downhill, brake until you reach a speed that is:
questions.explanation: Brake until your speed is 5 mph below your safe speed, then release the brake. Repeat this process as you go downhill.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you slow down other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: When visibility is poor and you are near other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Use low beams when driving near other vehicles in poor visibility, such as dawn, dusk, or bad weather. High beams can blind other drivers.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: The supply pressure gauge shows the driver how much air pressure is in the vehicle's air tanks.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift to a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked correctly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: With a trailer attached, mirrors can only be adjusted correctly when the trailer is straight. Check mirror adjustment before every trip.
